sections.h2: Where is Mandan, North Dakota, and how is the city laid out?
sections.html:
Mandan sits on the west bank of the Missouri River, directly across from Bismarck, on the eastern edge of Morton County. It is the county seat and one of the two core cities of the Bismarck metropolitan area.

The city covers about 13.7 square miles at an elevation of roughly 1,647 feet. The Census Bureau counted 24,206 residents in 2020 and estimates 25,061 for July 1, 2025, which makes Mandan the eighth-most populous city in North Dakota. Interstate 94, Interstate 194 and North Dakota highways 6 and 1806 serve the city.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Mandan's neighborhoods?
sections.html:
Mandan began as a Northern Pacific Railroad work camp in December 1878 and took its present name when the post office returned to it in September 1879. On March 3, 1879 the post office moved to the railroad's city site, within blocks of the first depot at Main Street and Stark Avenue, which is today's Collins Avenue.

The land has a much longer record. A Mandan village known as Good Fur Robe stood at the base of Crying Hill and was recorded as early as 1738, and the city takes its name from the Mandan people, who are now part of the Three Affiliated Tribes. In 1873 the Army added a cavalry post at Fort Abraham Lincoln, about five miles south of the townsite. The fort was deactivated in 1892 and the site is now Fort Abraham Lincoln State Park.

A rail division headquarters opened in Mandan in 1881, and BNSF still runs the railroad facilities. For a seller, the practical point is that Mandan has a long-settled core, so the age of a house and of its wiring, plumbing and heating can vary a lot from block to block.

sections.h2: What does Mandan's climate mean for a house?
sections.html:
Mandan has a humid continental climate with large swings between seasons, and a buyer or inspector will look closely at the roof, the furnace and the foundation. Records since 1913 show a high of 115 degrees Fahrenheit in July and a low of minus 46 in both February and December.

  • January afternoons average about 22.5 degrees and nights about 2.7 degrees, so heating systems carry most of the winter load.
  • Average yearly precipitation is about 18.4 inches, with June the wettest month at roughly 3.4 inches.

Mandan's building department lists furnace changeouts and water heater changeouts among the jobs that need a permit. If you replaced either one without a permit, expect the question to come up when a buyer's inspector asks for paperwork.

Climate figures come from the 1991 to 2020 normals reproduced on Wikipedia.

sections.h2: Do I need permits to be in good shape for a Mandan sale?
sections.html:
You do not need a permit to sell, but unpermitted work is the most common thing that slows a Mandan sale once a buyer starts asking questions. The city's Building Department (701-667-3230) says a permit is required before work starts, and it explains the reason in terms of selling: a history of construction matters when you sell, refinance or insure a home.

According to the city's permit FAQ, a permit is required for:

  • any structural alteration, residential or commercial
  • residential construction exceeding $2,000
  • window replacements that change the window size
  • any structure larger than 120 square feet
  • furnace changeouts, water heater changeouts and fireplace installs
  • water and sewer hookups

Permits are not required for painting, carpeting, tiling, countertops, fences up to 8.5 feet, or swimming pools. A permit usually takes under an hour to issue, and inspections carry no extra charge. The city also tells owners to check any contractor's license through the North Dakota Secretary of State, which is worth doing before you pay for repairs ahead of a sale.

sections.h2: How do special assessments work when I sell a house in Mandan?
sections.html:
A special assessment is a charge the city levies on property that benefits from a public project, and an unpaid balance follows the property into a sale. Mandan uses assessments for street paving, water and sewer mains, sidewalks, curb and gutter, and also for weed cutting, snow removal and diseased tree removal.

The city's special assessment page lays out the process. Costs for water, sewer and street projects are generally spread over 15 years, while repairs to private water or sewer lines and tree removal are typically spread over five. Weed cutting and delinquent utility bills carry a 10 percent administrative fee. The city auditor certifies each year's installment to the county by November 1, and owners can pay without interest through February 15 of the following year.

  • Search an address or parcel on the city's Special Assessment Inquiry Dashboard. If the parcel does not appear, there are no specials on it.
  • Call 701-667-3271 for payoff figures, or visit the Auditor's Office at 205 2nd Avenue NW.
  • For rural parcels outside city limits, Morton County handles balances at 701-667-3326.

Ask for the payoff figure before you accept any offer, because the amount is deducted from your proceeds at closing.

sections.h2: How is property tax calculated and paid on a Mandan home?
sections.html:
Morton County bills the tax, and the state sets the formula. The assessor first sets a true and full value, which for a home is market value. Assessed value is 50 percent of that, and the taxable value for residential property is 4.5 percent of the true and full value.

The State Tax Commissioner's residential property tax page gives a worked example: a $275,000 home in an area with 250 total mills has a taxable value of $12,375 and owes $3,095. Your own levy depends on the city, school district and other taxing entities that cover your parcel.

StepWhat happens in Morton County
StatementsMailed each December, and by statute by December 26
Discount5 percent off consolidated tax if paid by February 15; postmark accepted
Payable without penaltyUntil March 1, per the State Tax Commissioner
Questions on valueMorton County Tax Equalization Office, 701-667-3325
AppealsState Property Tax division, 701-328-3127, with a questionnaire and evidence

The county notes that failing to receive a bill does not remove the obligation to pay. Credits for primary residence, homestead and disabled veterans are listed on the state's residential page, and it is worth claiming one before a sale if you still qualify.

sections.h2: What do I have to disclose, and how does Mandan recording work?
sections.html:
North Dakota requires written disclosures from sellers, and the rules depend on who is involved in the sale. Under N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1, a seller of a residential dwelling with up to four units must give the buyer a written disclosure of material facts before the buyer signs final acceptance. Sales by a fiduciary administering an estate, sales through foreclosure, and transfers to close family are among the exceptions.

  • Radon: section 47-10-02.2 requires you to disclose in writing what you know about radon concentrations and to hand over any past test results or mitigation records.
  • Homeowners associations: section 47-10-02.3 requires association documents and fee information within ten days of signing.
  • Deeds: section 47-10-07 requires each deed to contain the post office address of every grantee.

The Morton County Recorder files the deed and keeps the land records that feed the county's tax rolls. The office also runs a free Property Fraud Alert that notifies an owner whenever a document is recorded against a property. Read the statute text at the North Dakota legislature's Title 47 chapter 10.

sections.h2: What are my options for selling a Mandan house quickly?
sections.html:
Mandan sellers generally choose among three routes: list with an agent, sell the house yourself, or accept a cash offer from a buyer who purchases as-is. Each has a different timeline and a different set of costs that fall on you.

A traditional listing can reach the widest buyer pool, but it usually involves showings, inspection requests and financing that depends on an appraisal. A cash purchase removes the lender step, and the buyer takes the house in its present condition, which suits a home with deferred maintenance, an unpermitted addition, or a tenant in place. If you are weighing a cash offer, compare the net amount you would receive after payoff of any special assessments, taxes and liens, not just the headline number.

Cash Home Buyers does not promise a price on this page. We can review a Mandan address and explain how an offer would be built, and you owe nothing if you turn it down.

faqs.q: Is Mandan the county seat of Morton County?
faqs.a: Yes. Mandan was designated the county seat in 1881, and the county courthouse and the Recorder, Treasurer and Tax Equalization offices are in the city. That means deed recording and property tax questions for a Mandan house are handled in your own city.

faqs.q: When are Mandan property taxes due?
faqs.a: Morton County mails statements each December, and the State Tax Commissioner says real property tax is payable without penalty until March 1. A 5 percent discount applies when the consolidated tax is paid in full by February 15, and a postmark counts as proof of timely payment.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to replace a furnace or water heater in Mandan?
faqs.a: Yes. The Mandan Building Department lists furnace and water heater changeouts among the work that requires a permit. Call 701-667-3230 if you are unsure about another project.

faqs.q: Who pays special assessments when a Mandan house is sold?
faqs.a: The balance is tied to the parcel, and who pays it at closing depends on the purchase contract, so settle that in writing. Request a payoff from the city Auditor's Office at 701-667-3271 before you accept an offer.

faqs.q: Do I have to give a buyer a disclosure form in North Dakota?
faqs.a: For a residential dwelling of up to four units, yes in most sales. N.D.C.C. 47-10-02.1 requires a written disclosure of material facts, and 47-10-02.2 adds a radon disclosure. Estate fiduciaries, foreclosure sales and certain family transfers are exempt from the main disclosure form.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mandan house with unpermitted work?
faqs.a: You can, but a buyer or lender may ask for documentation. A buyer that purchases as-is decides whether to accept the risk, and you should still tell the buyer what you know about the work.
